v.rationale: Both implementations pass their own suites and share a sound core: a conditional-update claim in markAsPaid, afterCommit dispatch, a global 5/s RateLimited middleware, Retry-After handling, backoff with retryUntil, and an idempotency key. impl-1 is stronger on the reliability details the task stresses. It skips cancelled or unpaid orders before the rate limiter. It sends the email exactly once and recovers if a send fails. It never marks an already-shipped order as failed. It fails fast on permanent 4xx errors so the partner isn't hammered. Its tests are broader and well organised. impl-2 is simpler but has confirmed bugs. failed() overwrites a sent order with failed. A failure to queue the email after the reference is saved means the customer is never emailed. A 401 is retried as if it were transient. Unpaid orders aren't guarded. impl-1's extra service class, exceptions and notified_at column are mild over-engineering, but they buy real correctness, so it ranks first.
